item.title: The most important team at the Olympics isn't a country. It's the timekeepers.
item.description: In the Winter Olympics, athlete careers are forever altered by that tiny difference determined by the most important team at the Olympics you don't know about — the Omega timekeepers.

item.title: From the sports desk: A new Olympic ‘cheating’ storyline
item.description: Hello from Milan and Cortina, where every day brings a fresh batch of surprises.

item.title: Team USA wins 5 medals on Day 4 of Milan Cortina Olympics
item.description: Team USA won medals in curling, skiing and luge on the fourth day of the Milan Cortina Olympics. Figure skater Ilia Malinin dazzled in his short program, and is currently leading the field in men’s singles. NBC News’ Tom Llamas reports.

item.title: DOJ fails to indict in case of Democrats' video about refusing illegal military orders
item.description: President Donald Trump had accused six lawmakers of "seditious behavior" after they urged members of the military to refuse unlawful orders in a video.

item.title: 10 people dead, including suspect, in British Columbia mass shooting
item.description: Police in Canada say a gunman killed seven people at a school in Tumbler Ridge, British Columbia, secondary school, while two others were found dead at a residence believed to be connected to the campus shooting. The suspected shooter was also found dead from an apparent self-inflicted gunshot wound, the agency said.

item.title: White House calls disappearance of Nancy Guthrie a 'heartbreaking situation'
item.description: White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt said that President Trump was following the developments in the search for Nancy Guthrie as authorities released new images and videos of a possible subject. NBC News' Gabe Gutierrez reports on the White House's reaction to what they are calling a "heartbreaking situation."

item.title: Why authorities are now releasing photos and videos in Nancy Guthrie case
item.description: NBC News’ Liz Kreutz explains why authorities are able to release photos and videos of a potential subject in Nancy Guthrie’s disappearance, more than a week after she was reported missing.

item.title: FBI launches new website on Nancy Guthrie case
item.description: The FBI launched a new website devoted to all of the elements that they have released in the disappearance case of Nancy Guthrie. NBC News’ Kelly O'Donnell details how this may help the investigation.

item.title: Investigators wrangled video from Nancy Guthrie’s Google Nest camera out of ‘backend systems’
item.description: Shortly after Nancy Guthrie disappeared, Pima County, Arizona, Sheriff Chris Nanos said that a camera affixed to her door had been disconnected, that she did not have a subscription that would have saved video and that investigators were trying to work with a tech company on the difficult forensic task of recovering any video

item.title: What the detainment in the Guthrie case could mean for the investigation
item.description: A person was detained for questioning in relation to the kidnapping of Nancy Guthrie. NBC News' Tom Winter reports on what this could mean for the case and if the detainment brings the investigation any closer to finding Guthrie.
